collection: NCEE National Values Education: self-discipline and good neighbourliness
note: Original four-option practice for final-year primary learners, using the 2026 component notice and provisional historical topic references. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain and apply self-control and responsible habits in school situations.
questions.prompt: Amina plans to finish her drawing before the library closes. Her friends invite her to join a game halfway through the work. What shows self-discipline?
questions.answer: Agree on a time to join them after finishing the drawing.
options: Agree on a time to join them after finishing the drawing.
Leave the drawing and ask a friend to complete it.
Keep drawing only until the teacher leaves.
Stop working and hide the unfinished drawing.
questions.explanation: Amina can keep both plans by following through on the task she set herself before joining the game.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain and apply self-control and responsible habits in school situations.
questions.prompt: Every pupil in a reading group remembers to bring a book. Yet the group often runs out of time because pupils spend the first ten minutes choosing who will read. Which routine would address the delay?
questions.answer: Let the fastest reader choose a new book for everyone.
options: Post a reading order before the meeting begins.
Let the fastest reader choose a new book for everyone.
Ask pupils to bring two books instead of one.
Send a reminder to bring books the evening before.
questions.explanation: The books already arrive. Agreeing the order in advance removes the decision that uses up reading time.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain and apply self-control and responsible habits in school situations.
questions.prompt: Kene finds it hard to hear instructions because he often starts chatting while the teacher speaks. Which habit would help him change his own behaviour?
questions.answer: Ask a friend to copy the instructions for him every day.
options: Wait for the teacher to speak more loudly.
Keep his questions until the teacher pauses and note the main steps as he listens.
Ask a friend to copy the instructions for him every day.
Sit farther from the board so he can talk more freely.
questions.explanation: Waiting for a pause and noting key steps give Kene specific actions he can practise each time.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain and apply self-control and responsible habits in school situations.
questions.prompt: Two pupils check their own spelling after writing. One rereads the words in the same order and misses the same errors. Which change would make the check more useful?
questions.answer: Copy all the words from a classmate’s list first.
options: Check only the words that look familiar.
Spend longer looking at the title.
Compare each doubtful word with a dictionary and fix any mismatch.
Copy all the words from a classmate’s list first.
questions.explanation: An independent reference tests whether the spelling is right instead of relying on the same memory that produced it.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain and apply self-control and responsible habits in school situations.
questions.prompt: A team is asked to return library books on Friday. Bisi is away on Friday and learns this on Tuesday. What responsible step should she take?
questions.answer: Arrange with the librarian to return her books before Friday.
options: Arrange with the librarian to return her books before Friday.
Keep the books until the next lending day because she will be away.
Hand the books to any pupil without saying when they are due.
Ask the other team members to delay their returns too.
questions.explanation: Making an arrangement early lets Bisi meet the shared deadline despite her absence.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain and apply self-control and responsible habits in school situations.
questions.prompt: A pupil promises to feed the class fish after lessons but remembers only when she sees the food container. The container must stay in a locked cupboard. Which change would best help her keep the routine?
questions.answer: Put more food in the cupboard.
options: Set a reminder at the place where she collects her bag.
Put more food in the cupboard.
Feed the fish twice whenever she remembers.
Choose a different cupboard for the food each day.
questions.explanation: Seeing a reminder in a place she visits every day can prompt the task while the food remains safely stored.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose considerate actions and reason about effects on neighbours.
questions.prompt: A neighbour who works at night sleeps in the afternoon. Children need a place to practise their drum routine. What should the children do first?
questions.answer: Stop practising for the rest of the term.
options: Practise beside the neighbour’s window for a shorter time.
Ask the neighbour when the noise would disturb them least.
Stop practising for the rest of the term.
Ask other neighbours to vote on whether the worker should sleep.
questions.explanation: An agreed time can allow the group to practise while respecting the neighbour’s need to rest.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose considerate actions and reason about effects on neighbours.
questions.prompt: Water running from one household’s roof crosses a shared path and makes it slippery after rain. Which response addresses the source of the problem?
questions.answer: Ask people to walk more slowly on the path.
options: Close the path permanently to visitors.
Dry the path once without discussing the runoff.
Agree on a safe way to direct the runoff away from the path.
Ask people to walk more slowly on the path.
questions.explanation: Redirecting the runoff keeps it from repeatedly making the path slippery, while drying or walking slowly leaves its cause in place.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose considerate actions and reason about effects on neighbours.
questions.prompt: The residents of a compound want to decide where to keep a shared waste bin. One household has difficulty walking far. Which plan is considerate and practical?
questions.answer: Discuss a reachable spot that also keeps entrances clear.
options: Discuss a reachable spot that also keeps entrances clear.
Put the bin closest to the household that complained first.
Choose the farthest corner so only visitors have to pass it.
Allow each household to move the bin whenever it wants.
questions.explanation: An accessible location and an unobstructed entrance address the needs of different people using the compound.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose considerate actions and reason about effects on neighbours.
questions.prompt: Two neighbours disagree about who damaged a flower pot while sweeping the compound. Neither saw it break. Which approach is fairest?
questions.answer: Ask the person who swept first to pay automatically.
options: Check what each person actually observed before deciding how to put things right.
Ask the person who swept first to pay automatically.
Charge the household that owns the most pots.
Decide according to which neighbour has lived there longer.
questions.explanation: Actual observations are better evidence than sweeping order or seniority. The neighbours can discuss a fair solution once they know what happened.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose considerate actions and reason about effects on neighbours.
questions.prompt: Akwaugo’s family borrows a ladder. She notices a loose rung before anyone uses it. What should the family do?
questions.answer: Return it quietly because the rung was already loose.
options: Put it by the fence where another neighbour can borrow it.
Tell the owner about the loose rung and keep others from using it until it is safe.
Return it quietly because the rung was already loose.
Ask a younger child to test the rung for them.
questions.explanation: Telling the owner lets them address the defect and prevents another borrower from using a dangerous ladder.

questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.learningObjective: Choose considerate actions and reason about effects on neighbours.
questions.prompt: Households share a noticeboard for compound news. Several people miss important notices because large adverts cover them. What change would most directly make the board work for everyone?
questions.answer: Ask residents to print larger copies of all adverts.
options: Take every notice down at the end of each day.
Give the household nearest the board all the space.
Reserve a marked area for important notices and agree when old notices come down.
Ask residents to print larger copies of all adverts.
questions.explanation: Reserved space keeps shared announcements visible, and removing outdated notices stops the board from becoming crowded again.
